newsitem.title: USA: SEC to offer relief on order entry rules.
newsitem.headline: SEC to offer relief on order entry rules.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) will likely offer securities firms a grace period to implement some of its more complicated new order entry rules, a top commission regulator said on Monday.
Speaking at a briefing, SEC director of market regulation Richard Lindsey told traders they would get several months to adopt some of the new policies.
Lindsey said the SEC would soon issue "no action" letters exempting firms for whom technology issues stood in the way of meeting some rules.

Among the rules, which go into effect January 10, 1997, are requirements to display customer limit orders within 30 seconds of receipt and to indicate whether non standard quotes have been rounded and by how much.
Lindsey said firms whose trading system upgrades will not be finished by the deadline will likely get several months to complete the work.
He also said the SEC planned a more gradual phase in of the new display requirements.
Under new guidelines, the 50 most liquid stocks on Nasdaq would be subject to full display rules on January 10, 1997, and another 100 by January 31, 1997.
The SEC had previously planned to subject 1,000 securities to the rule on January 10, 1997. All 3,000 Nasdaq securities are expected to be covered by the rule by August 1997.
